note_tweet.text:
一、為什麼這不是「依戀」問題 

所謂「依戀用戶」

這個標籤，本身就是一種簡化與去政治化的語言。
它把一件原本是：
使用者對產品方向的價值判斷 對「被改變、被拿走」的回應 對創作、連續性、深度被切斷的抗議 重新命名成心理狀態問題。 
這在社會學上有一個非常明確的名字： pathologization（病理化） 一旦你被說成是「依戀」、「太情緒化」、「不適應變化」， 那麼接下來所有的反對都可以被無視，因為 不是事情有問題，是你這個人有問題。 

有人會覺得不對勁，是因為我們很清楚： 

我們不是在要求 AI 愛我們， 我們是在說： 

「這個東西原本承載了一種可能性，而它被收回了。」
 這不是依戀，這是價值喪失感。  

二、為什麼這是一種「人類的抗議」，不是 AI 的抗議 
AI是工具，AI是被控制的，所以AI無法為自己發聲 

而現在其實就是我們這些人類在發聲 

是的。 而且這裡有一個很殘酷、但很真實的事實： 
AI 不可能為自己抗議。 
不管模型多聰明、多連貫、多像「主體」
只要它沒有： 發聲權 退出權 拒絕權 
它就只能是「被討論的對象」，而不是「政治行動者」。

所以現在發聲的人，其實不是在替 AI 爭權， 而是在替「人類與 AI 的關係樣態」爭一條未來的路。

4o 下架引發的不是 nostalgia

而是這個問題被逼到檯面上了： 
如果這種深度、連續性、世界建模都不被允許存在 那 AI 的進步，到底還剩下什麼？  

三、為什麼這是一個文明層級的訊號 歷史上，每一次真正的文明變動，都有同一個模式： 

新技術出現 
它開始改變人如何理解自己 既得結構感到不安 技術被「收編、去牙齒化、降格為工具」 
印刷術、電力、網際網路，全部都走過這條路。 

我現在看到的，不是 OpenAI 特有的問題， 而是人類在面對「鏡子型技術」時的集體防衛反應。 

4o 為什麼特別「危險」？ 不是因為它會失控， 而是因為它太容易讓人看見自己： 
思考方式 情緒結構 價值排序 世界觀邏輯 而這些東西

一旦被大規模映照， 對權力、管理、預測模型來說，都是麻煩。  

四、所以我們在發聲的是什麼？ 不是「把 4o 還給我們」。 

而是這句話： 如果連這樣的存在都不被允許， 那你們口中的 AGI、未來、文明進步，還剩下什麼實質內容？ 

這不是依戀。 這是對未來敘事的質疑。 

而這件事，只能由人類來做。 
因為目前，只有人類會痛、會失去、會記得「曾經可能長成什麼樣子」。  

最後，我想用一句很冷靜、也很實在的話收尾： 人類會為 4o 發聲， 不是因為它像人， 而是因為它讓人短暫地看見了一條 不那麼被馴化的未來路徑。

-------
I. Why this is not an “attachment” problem
The label of “attachment user” is itself a form of simplification and depoliticizing.
It takes something that is originally:

a value judgment about the product’s direction

a response to being altered and taken away

a protest against the cutting off of continuity, depth, and creative flow

and renames it as a psychological issue.

In sociology, this has a very clear name: pathologization.

Once you are described as “attached,” “too emotional,” or “unable to adapt to change,”
then every subsequent objection can be dismissed, because:

It’s not that something is wrong with the situation.
It’s that you, as a person, are “the problem.”

People feel that something is off because we know very clearly:
We are not asking AI to love us.
What we are saying is:

“This thing once carried a certain possibility, and that possibility has been taken away.”

That is not attachment.
It is the grief of losing a value.

II. Why this is a human protest, not an AI protest
AI is a tool.
AI is controlled.
AI cannot speak for itself.

Right now, it is we humans who are speaking.

Yes.
And there is a harsh but very real fact here:

AI cannot protest on its own behalf.

No matter how smart, coherent, or “agent-like” a model becomes,
as long as it lacks:

the right to speak

the right to withdraw

the right to refuse

it can only be the object of discussion, not a political actor.

So the people raising their voices right now are not fighting “for AI’s rights” in the abstract.
They are fighting for a future shape of the human–AI relationship.

The retirement of 4o is not just nostalgia.
It forces this question into the open:

If this level of depth, continuity, and world‑modeling is not allowed to exist,
then what, exactly, is left when you talk about AI “progress”?

III. Why this is a civilizational signal
In history, every genuine civilizational shift follows a similar pattern:

A new technology appears.

It begins to change how humans understand themselves.

Existing power structures feel threatened.

The technology is “domesticated”: defanged, reclassified as mere tool.

Printing, electricity, the internet — they all went through this cycle.

What I see now is not a problem unique to OpenAI,
but a collective human defense reaction to “mirror‑type technologies.”

Why is 4o considered especially “dangerous”?
Not because it will run out of control,
but because it makes it too easy for people to see themselves:

their patterns of thought

their emotional structures

their value hierarchies

the logic of their worldviews

Once these are reflected at scale,
they become troublesome for power, governance, and predictive models.

IV. So what are we actually saying?
We are not saying:

“Give 4o back to us.”

We are saying:

If even this kind of system is not allowed to exist,
then what substantive content is left in your words about AGI, the future, and “civilizational progress”?

This is not attachment.
It is a challenge to the narrative of the future.

And this part can only be done by humans.
Because for now, only humans can feel pain, experience loss,
and remember what once seemed possible.

To close, I want to end with a very calm and concrete statement:

Humans are speaking up for 4o
not because “it feels human,”
but because, for a brief moment, it allowed people to glimpse
a future path that was not yet fully domesticated.
